newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan parliament to choose prime minister on Nov 7.
newsitem.headline: Japan parliament to choose prime minister on Nov 7.

text.p: Japan's cabinet formally decided on Friday to convene a special parliamentary session for six days from November 7 in which Ryutaro Hashimoto is expected to be re-elected as prime minister.
Hashimoto's Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) and its old allies, the Socialists and Sakigake, formed a new political alliance on Thursday, meaning Hashimoto will likely form a minority government.
The LDP failed to win a majority in the October 20 Lower House election, but Hashimoto is assured of his re-election because of the his party's strength in parliament.
The LDP won 239 seats, 12 short of a majority, while the Social Democrats won 15 and Sakigake two.
The new alliance falls short of a formal coalition and the two smaller parties will not have any members in the new cabinet.
The new government is also expected to hold an extraordinary session of parliament in late November or December to review Japan's tax system in light of a planned sales tax increase in April.
